Compare md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:202-207 and md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:219-223 (blocked = waiting, event emitted).

findings.title: 'Resumable review' classifiers are keyed on task.error, which LangGraph never records for KeyboardInterrupt; their real trigger re-executes a deterministic failure
findings.detail: Both PRs justify resumable_review/review_resumable as the path by which a Ctrl-C'd review re-enters its running session. The installed LangGraph runner commits a task error only inside `except Exception`, so KeyboardInterrupt leaves the review task pending with no error and the next drive() loop re-invokes it naturally; the classifier is not what makes the (passing) [75,130,75,0] tests work. The only way task.error is set while the receipt is still 'launching'/'running' is an Exception raised in review_candidate's prologue or review_worktree (e.g. validate_bundle or 'Reviewer worktree changed'), and then the classifier returns True and the same failure is re-run on every supervisor restart up to the 45 limit, the opposite of 'ambiguous invocations never replay'. PR 9 also placed it inside advance_failed_checks whose docstring says 'never launches or review'. PR 11 has no such classifier and would fail closed.
findings.evidence: .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/langgraph/pregel/_runner.py:221-223 `self.commit(t, None)` / `except Exception as exc: self.commit(t, exc)`; _runner.py:578-600 commit() only writes ERROR for exceptions it receives. md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:343-352 resumable_review, :355 docstring 'Retry only recorded failing verification packets, never launches or review.' vs :362 `if failures == ["review"]: return resumable_review(runtime)`; test_automatic.py:263-285 builds `SimpleNamespace(name="review", error="interrupted")` synthetically. md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:216-226 review_resumable, :459 wired into drive; `grep -n review_resumable test_automatic.py` -> no direct test.

findings.title: wait_review's stop-marker recovery shortcut is unreachable in the real flow
findings.detail: wait_review starts with 'if review.stop.json says stopped, accept the file bound to the stopped session'. But review_native always calls runtime.sessions.run_reviewer first, which for an existing receipt calls reconcile() -> locate(); for a stopped session locate() returns None or raises 'No live native PID', so run_reviewer raises 'Existing launch cannot be reconciled' before wait_review is ever entered. The branch documents a recovery that cannot happen. PR 11 handles the same scenario correctly by returning early from review_candidate on a succeeded receipt and retrying only the stop.
findings.evidence: md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:194-198 `stop = runtime.directory / f"{REVIEW_NODE}.stop.json"; if stop.exists() and read_json(stop)["stopped"]: return read_review_completion(...)`; review_native order :286 run_reviewer -> :297 wait_review; interactive.py:175-176 `if (...review.interactive.json).exists(): return self.reconcile(REVIEW_NODE)`; reconcile :123-125 `row = self.locate(...); if row is None: raise RuntimeError("Existing launch cannot be reconciled; no automatic relaunch")`. Compare md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:236-241.

findings.title: export_state bumped to 1.2.0 while the adapter still requires z.literal('1.0.0') (outside the slice-A file set, verified)
findings.detail: Not part of the five controller files, but it decides whether the merged branch is usable: any run exported after merging PR 10 is rejected by server/projects.ts until slice B lands. PR 9 leaves export_state untouched; PR 11 updates the adapter to accept 1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0.
findings.evidence: md-manager-high/workflow/export_state.py:16 `EXPORT_VERSION = "1.2.0"`; `git -C md-manager-high diff 61e4752 --stat -- server/ src/` -> empty; md-manager/server/projects.ts:37 `const EXPORT_VERSION = '1.0.0'`, :52 `version: z.literal(EXPORT_VERSION)`. md-manager-ultra/server/projects.ts:44 `const EXPORT_VERSIONS = ['1.0.0', '1.1.0', '1.2.0'] as const`.

findings.title: The missing-key default is stated three ways: DEFAULTS says native, two literals say print
findings.detail: reviewer_transport() and validate_automatic each hard-code "print" as the fallback while DEFAULTS["reviewer_transport"] is "native". The choice itself is the safest of the three PRs for the on-disk run (its plan has no key and was print-reviewed), but a maintainer reading DEFAULTS will 'fix' the getter. PR 9 reads DEFAULTS in one place; PR 11 also hard-codes its literal.
findings.evidence: md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:26 `... "reviewer_transport": "native"}`, :45 `return plan["automatic"].get("reviewer_transport", "print")`, :54 `settings.get("reviewer_transport", "print") not in TRANSPORTS`; :53 `set(settings) - {"reviewer_transport"} != set(DEFAULTS) - {"reviewer_transport"}`. Live plan: ~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/project-workflows/project-workflows-001/plan.json automatic = {finish, permission_mode, worker_timeout_seconds: 3600, review_timeout_seconds: 1800} (no key), review.stdout.json present (print mode). Contrast md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:43-44 `return plan.get("automatic", {}).get("reviewer_transport", DEFAULTS["reviewer_transport"])`.

findings.title: automatic.py now depends on interactive.py panes and bypasses the Pipeline.launch wrapper convention; completion bound to a self-reported session UUID
findings.detail: Baseline layering is sessions -> interactive -> pipeline, with automatic.py using only sessions and the Pipeline runtime; Pipeline.launch(node) wraps sessions.run with events. PR 10 imports REVIEW_NODE and attach_reviewer_pane into automatic.py at module level, calls runtime.sessions.run_reviewer directly and emits the launch/pane events from automatic.py, so the reviewer launch has no Pipeline counterpart to launch(). PR 9 and PR 11 add Pipeline.launch_reviewer mirroring launch(). PR 10 also asks the reviewer to write its own session UUID (reviewer_session) rather than a controller-issued launch_token as the workers do; it worked in the smoke run but relies on the model knowing its own id.
findings.evidence: md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:21 `from .interactive import REVIEW_NODE, attach_reviewer_pane`; :286-296 run_reviewer + runtime.event(REVIEW_NODE, "interactive", ...) + attach_reviewer_pane inside review_native; :159 prompt example `"reviewer_session": "<your own session UUID as shown by `claude agents`; the controller verifies it>"`; :184 `if item["reviewer_session"] != session_id`. Smoke: ~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/smoke/review-smoke-001/review.completion.json reviewer_session 5865c9a6-... == review.interactive.json session_id. Compare md-manager-opus/workflow/pipeline.py:156-171 and md-manager-ultra/workflow/pipeline.py:148-167 Pipeline.launch_reviewer.

findings.title: automatic.py never imports REVIEW and spells the node and its files as ~20 magic strings while pipeline.py uses the constant; label rule duplicated inline
findings.detail: interactive.py defines REVIEW = "review" and pipeline.py imports it, but automatic.py uses literal "review" for locate(), event(), node_id binding and the file names review.interactive.json / review.completion.json / review.stop.json / review.json. A rename or a file-layout change has to be chased through two conventions. The pane/launch label rule 'reviewer' if node == REVIEW else node is also written twice instead of once (PR 10 has PANE_LABELS).
findings.evidence: grep -n '"review' md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py -> :162, :163, :185, :198, :209, :211, :216, :223, :271, :283, :302, :314, :332, :345, :355, :362, :473 (no `from .interactive import REVIEW`; imports at :20-21 are checks/sessions only). md-manager-ultra/workflow/interactive.py:38 `f"workflow-{...}-{'reviewer' if node == REVIEW else node}"` and :353 `f"Claude: {'reviewer' if node == REVIEW else node}"`. Compare md-manager-high/workflow/interactive.py:26 PANE_LABELS used at :41 and :334.

findings.title: Densest control flow of the three: nested resume branch, 15-line KeyboardInterrupt handler that re-reads receipts, BaseException re-raise idiom
findings.detail: review_candidate carries an inline three-way resume decision (succeeded-but-unstopped / running-without-session_id -> reconcile_reviewer with its own error handling / running-with-session -> _accept_native); _review_native's except KeyboardInterrupt reads review.interactive.json to copy session_id/background_id into the review receipt; Pipeline.launch_reviewer catches BaseException, logs, then re-raises only non-Exception, and pre-checks HERDR_ENV although observer.herdr() already guards it. Every branch is tested and the behaviour is arguably the most correct, but a maintainer must hold four interrupt points and two receipts in their head to change any of it. PR 10 handles the same happy path plus Ctrl-C in about half the lines.
findings.evidence: md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:228-260 review_candidate resume block (`if not receipt.get("session_id"): try: bound = runtime.reconcile_reviewer() except Exception as error: receipt.update(status="needs_reconciliation"...)`), :298-316 `except KeyboardInterrupt: issued = runtime.directory / "review.interactive.json" ... bound = read_json(issued); receipt.update({key: bound[key] for key in ("session_id", "background_id") if bound.get(key)}, status="running")`; pipeline.py:156-167 `if (self.directory / "terminals.json").exists() and os.environ.get("HERDR_ENV") == "1": ... except BaseException as error: ... if not isinstance(error, Exception): raise`; observer.py:44-45 already raises when HERDR_ENV != "1". funclen: _accept_native 39, _review_native 32, review_candidate ~45 lines.

findings.title: Hand-written reviewCompletion.schema.json with no v1.ts/examples/contract test breaks the contracts:export convention
findings.detail: Every other schema in contracts/workflow is generated from v1.ts (zod) with examples and contract tests; PR 9 and PR 10 followed that. PR 11's 39-line JSON has no TypeScript source, so the completion contract now has a different source of truth from the rest, and the cross-field rules (blocked-needs-findings, approved-cannot-carry-unresolved-P0/P1) exist only in Python (blocking_findings/_decide), not in the contract package.
findings.evidence: md-manager-ultra/contracts/workflow/reviewCompletion.schema.json (hand-written, `"title": "Review completion signal v1.0.0"`); `grep -c reviewCompletion md-manager-ultra/contracts/workflow/{v1.ts,examples.ts,contract.test.ts}` -> 0,0,0. Compare md-manager-opus/contracts/workflow/v1.ts:94-107 reviewCompletionSchema + :169-177 validateReviewCompletion and md-manager-high/contracts/workflow/v1.ts:110-120.

findings.title: Pane attach split across three functions, a redirect branch inside attach_panels, and a non-idempotent attach_reviewer_panel
findings.detail: attach_panels now begins with 'if a mapping exists and the reviewer is missing, go do the reviewer instead', and ends with a second reviewer-allocation branch; attach_reviewer_panel raises if the reviewer pane already exists, whereas PR 9/10 return the mapping. Pipeline.launch_reviewer swallows that error into a 'not attached' event, so a second call reports a misleading failure rather than a no-op.
findings.evidence: md-manager-ultra/workflow/interactive.py:291-296 `if set(NODES) <= set(mapping) and REVIEW not in mapping and (directory / "review.interactive.json").exists(): return attach_reviewer_panel(sessions)` inside attach_panels; :338-340 second branch `if (directory / "review.interactive.json").exists() and sessions.locate(REVIEW, rows) is not None: allocate_reviewer_pane(...)`; :371-372 `if REVIEW in mapping: raise RuntimeError("Reviewer pane already allocated; ...")`. Compare md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:367-368 `if REVIEWER in mapping: return mapping` and md-manager-high/workflow/interactive.py:349-350.

findings.title: _decide rewrites the reviewer's verdict before persisting review.json
findings.detail: An approved verdict with an unresolved P0/P1 is persisted as verdict "blocked"; the record the viewer shows is no longer what the reviewer wrote (the original survives only in receipt["decision"]). PR 10 persists the verdict verbatim and raises.
findings.evidence: md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:280-283 `blocked = decision["verdict"] != "approved" or bool(blocking_findings(decision["findings"])); if blocked: review["verdict"] = "blocked"  # An approval with an unresolved P0/P1 is contradictory; the run is blocked.` then :284 `save_json(runtime.directory / "review.json", review)`. Compare md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:270-276.

findings.title: Default 'native' for plans lacking reviewer_transport does not describe any real plan; PR 11's docstring claim is unenforced
findings.detail: automatic_settings pins the key on every new plan, so the only plans without it are pre-existing ones, all reviewed in print mode. PR 9 and PR 11 default the getter to native (PR 11's docstring adds 'though they never launch a new reviewer', which nothing enforces: an old plan still at the review step would launch a native reviewer whose preflight never checked --allowedTools). PR 10's 'print' default matches reality; PR 11 at least records the truth in the export via recorded_transport().
findings.evidence: md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:43-44 default DEFAULTS["reviewer_transport"] == "native"; md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:58-60 `"""Effective transport: plans that predate the setting are native, though they never launch a new reviewer.""" return plan["automatic"].get("reviewer_transport", "native")`; md-manager-ultra/workflow/export_state.py:62-76, :147-148 recorded_transport(). Live plan lacks the key and has review.stdout.json (print).

findings.title: Copy-pasted prompt instruction and a new event status vocabulary word
findings.detail: The reviewer prompt tells a Write-only session (no Bash) to write 'atomically (temporary file then rename)', copied from the worker completion_prompt where Bash exists; PR 11 explicitly says the opposite because its allow-rule is path-specific. Pipeline.launch_reviewer also introduces a new event status 'detached'; the adapter tolerates unknown statuses (maps to null) but it is a new word in the timeline vocabulary that no contract or viewer knows.

findings.title: write_private/prompt.txt evidence added to the shared interactive.py surface as part of slice A
findings.detail: Persisting worker and reviewer prompts is slice C (run inputs) material; PR 11 lands it in the shared launch path. Harmless (three lines) but it widens what slice A touches in the most shared file.
findings.evidence: md-manager-ultra/workflow/interactive.py:181-182 `# The exact prompt is run evidence (the viewer shows it)... write_private(self.directory / f"{node}.prompt.txt", prompt)`, :213 `write_private(self.directory / "review.prompt.txt", prompt)`, :241-243 def write_private.

findings.title: reconcile()/launch() extraction and finish_review are the cleanest generalisation on the shared surface
findings.detail: The common native-session lifecycle exists once: launch() fills node_id/session_id/plan_digest/worktree/status/attempt/launcher_invocations/launch_requested_at and owns the log/fsync/settle/needs_reconciliation handling; run() and run_reviewer() only build a command and a 2-key receipt. finish_review is the single acceptance path for both transports and fixes the baseline's severity-only P0/P1 check. SESSION_NODES/PANE_LABELS keep one identity; launched_nodes() lets status/attach scale to N sessions; attach_reviewer_pane returns None for headless runs instead of throwing.
findings.evidence: md-manager-high/workflow/interactive.py:117-129 reconcile, :131-161 launch (`receipt.update(node_id=node, session_id=None, plan_digest=plan_digest(self.plan), worktree=str(cwd), status="launching", attempt=1, launcher_invocations=1, launch_requested_at=...)`), :163-175 run_reviewer (`receipt = {"launch_token": None, "base_commit": ..., "role": "reviewer", ...}; return self.launch(REVIEW_NODE, cwd, command, receipt)`), :223-225 launched_nodes, :343-352 attach_reviewer_pane `return None`; automatic.py:264-280 finish_review with `any(x["severity"] in {"P0", "P1"} and x["disposition"] != "resolved" ...)`.

findings.title: Reusable validators and a precisely bounded stop-retry are the best-designed pieces in any of the three PRs
findings.detail: blocking_findings and check_review(require_approved) are shared by validate_review, _decide and ExportRuntime, so the finding rules exist once. reviewer_stopped/reviewer_stop_pending guard exactly the one retry that is safe (a durable accept whose stop was not confirmed), drive raises immediately with a resume note and only a resumed controller retries once. The variadic-flag ordering trap is explained at the command builder, and REQUIRED_KEYS/REVIEW_COMPLETION_LIMIT/REVIEWER_TRANSPORTS are named constants.
findings.evidence: md-manager-ultra/workflow/pipeline.py:42-70 blocking_findings/check_review, :382-384 validate_review delegates, :415-440 ExportRuntime reuses check_review(require_approved=False); automatic.py:269-273 reviewer_stopped, :467-478 reviewer_stop_pending, :530-540 drive `if reviewer_stop_pending(runtime, failed): raise RuntimeError(REVIEW_STOP_NOTE.format(...)) from error`; interactive.py:220-223 '--tools, --allowedTools and --add-dir are variadic: any of them directly before the positional prompt would swallow it'; automatic.py:26-28, :141.

findings.title: Single-source transport default, tidy settings validation, and the Pipeline.launch pattern honoured
findings.detail: transport() reads DEFAULTS rather than repeating a literal; validate_automatic uses REQUIRED_SETTINGS <= set(settings) <= set(DEFAULTS); review_worktree/review_instructions/review_completion_prompt are extracted; stop_session returns the intent for callers; attach_reviewer_pane is idempotent; Pipeline.launch_reviewer mirrors Pipeline.launch so events stay in one layer; the completion contract lives in v1.ts with cross-field rules and the Python mirror says so.
findings.evidence: md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:43-44, :49 `not REQUIRED_SETTINGS <= set(settings) <= set(DEFAULTS)`, :214-231 review_worktree, :183 comment 'Cross-field rules mirrored from contracts/workflow/v1.ts'; pipeline.py:112-140 stop_session returns intent, :156-171 launch_reviewer; interactive.py:355-382 attach_reviewer_pane `if REVIEWER in mapping: return mapping`; contracts/workflow/v1.ts:94-107, :169-177.

data.summary: I read the baseline workflow/{automatic,interactive,pipeline,launch,sessions}.py on main and the three slice-A diffs (pr9.diff, pr10-sliceA.diff, pr11-sliceA.diff), then the full files in each worktree where the diffs cut context, and checked reachability claims against the installed LangGraph 1.2.11 runner and the on-disk run. On the shared controller surface PR 10 produced the cleanest generalisation: it extracted InteractiveSessions.reconcile()/launch() so run() and run_reviewer() are thin composers, keeps one node identity ("review") with a PANE_LABELS map, and funnels both transports through one finish_review(). PR 11 reaches the same reconcile/launch split and adds the best reusable validators (check_review, blocking_findings, reviewer_stop_pending) but pays for its edge-case coverage with the densest control flow, ~20 magic "review" strings in automatic.py while pipeline.py uses a REVIEW constant, a duplicated label conditional, and a non-idempotent pane attach. PR 9 is the smallest diff but generalised the least: run_reviewer is a 54-line near-verbatim copy of run(), the acceptance block is duplicated across review_worktree/native_review/print_review, it carries a dual reviewer/review identity bridged by file_prefix() in sessions.py, and it ships a real bug where an approved verdict with a resolved P0/P1 is blocked, contradicting its own contract.
data.pr9: Structure: minimal and readable, but the generalisation stops at the surface. worktree()/receipt_path() (interactive.py:27-32) let locate()/attach-one serve the reviewer, yet run_reviewer (interactive.py:187-240, 54 lines) copies run() wholesale: the same reconcile block (plan-digest check, locate, receipt.update(status="attached_session_available"...)), the same launch-log/fsync/settle/needs_reconciliation block. Any fix to worker launch must be made twice. Naming: REVIEWER = "reviewer" lives in sessions.py:20 (a module whose ClaudeSessions.run still rejects it), while files, receipts, events, graph node and stop marker all use "review" via file_prefix() (sessions.py:23-25); attach-one takes --node reviewer, terminals.json key is "reviewer", node_id is "review". Two identities and a bridge function are the price. Acceptance logic duplicated 3x ("Reviewer worktree changed"/"Evidence changed during review" appear in review_worktree, native_review and print_review). Real bug: native_review (automatic.py:272) blocks any P0/P1 regardless of disposition while read_review_completion (:186-190) and the v1.ts cross-field rule only reject unresolved ones. wait_review raises on native state "blocked" with the worker's quota message (:208) although the reviewer runs dontAsk, where blocked means it needs a human; PR 10/11 both learned this live. resumable_review (:343-352) is wired into advance_failed_checks whose docstring says "never launches or review" (:355 vs :362) and is keyed on task.error, which LangGraph records only for Exception, so Ctrl-C never reaches it. Good parts: transport() reads DEFAULTS (single source, :43-44), REQUIRED_SETTINGS <= set <= DEFAULTS (:49), review_worktree/review_instructions extracted, stop_session returns intent (pipeline.py:112-140), attach_reviewer_pane is idempotent (interactive.py:367), Pipeline.launch_reviewer mirrors Pipeline.launch (pipeline.py:156-171), contract in v1.ts with cross-field rules mirrored. No live run, so the prompt still says "temporary file then rename" (:168) for a Write-only reviewer and the write permission is not allow-listed.
data.pr10: Structure: the best abstraction of the three on the shared surface. InteractiveSessions.reconcile(node) (interactive.py:117-129) and launch(node, cwd, command, receipt) (:131-161) hold the common receipt fields, log/fsync, settle and needs_reconciliation handling once; run() (:177-221) and run_reviewer() (:163-175) only build their command and a 2-key receipt. One identity: REVIEW_NODE = "review", SESSION_NODES, PANE_LABELS (:24-26); the reviewer/review split is a label map, not a second name. launched_nodes() (:223) generalises status/attach to N sessions and attach_panels splits panes in a loop (:319-325). finish_review (automatic.py:264-280) is the single acceptance path for both transports (one copy each of "Evidence changed", "Reviewer worktree changed", the review dict, and the P0/P1 check fixed to honour disposition); review.json is persisted for blocked verdicts (:274) so the viewer can show why; the reviewer is stopped on any non-interrupt failure (:311), mirroring the worker policy. attach_reviewer_pane returns None for a headless run (:343-352) instead of throwing. Weaknesses: automatic.py imports interactive at module level (:21) and emits pane events itself, bypassing the Pipeline.launch wrapper convention that PR 9/11 follow; reviewer_transport() and validate_automatic each hard-code "print" (:45, :54) while DEFAULTS says "native" (:26), so the module states the default three ways; the stop-marker shortcut in wait_review (:196-198) is unreachable because review_native calls run_reviewer -> reconcile -> locate first, which fails for a stopped session; review_resumable (:216-226) has the same LangGraph dead-trigger issue as PR 9 and no direct unit test; review_candidate grew to ~45 lines carrying worktree creation and resume checks. Binding the completion to a self-reported reviewer_session UUID (:159, :184) deviates from the worker launch_token pattern, though the smoke artifacts show it worked. Outside the slice-A file set but verified: export_state bumped to 1.2.0 with server/projects.ts still z.literal('1.0.0').
data.pr11: Structure: same reconcile()/launch() extraction as PR 10 (interactive.py:113-149) with run()/run_reviewer composing them, and the strongest reusable validators: blocking_findings and check_review(require_approved) (pipeline.py:42-70) serve validate_review, _decide and ExportRuntime alike; REQUIRED_KEYS, REVIEW_COMPLETION_LIMIT and REVIEWER_TRANSPORTS are named (automatic.py:26-28, :141). The one legitimate review retry (stop unconfirmed after a durable accept) is guarded precisely by reviewer_stopped/reviewer_stop_pending (:269-273, :467-478) and bounded in drive (:530-540); the CLI arg-order trap is explained where the command is built (interactive.py:220-223). Costs: automatic.py never imports REVIEW and uses ~20 literal "review", "review.interactive.json", "review.completion.json", "review.stop.json" strings (e.g. :185, :209, :216, :223, :271, :302, :332) while pipeline.py uses the constant; the label rule 'reviewer' if node == REVIEW else node is written twice (interactive.py:38, :353). Control flow is the densest of the three: review_candidate's nested resume branch (automatic.py:228-260) with inline reconcile error handling, a 15-line KeyboardInterrupt branch in _review_native that reads review.interactive.json to copy bound ids (:298-316), and Pipeline.launch_reviewer's except BaseException / if not isinstance(error, Exception): raise idiom plus a HERDR_ENV check that duplicates observer.herdr's own guard (pipeline.py:156-167). Pane attach is spread over allocate_reviewer_pane/attach_pane/attach_reviewer_panel with a redirect branch at the top of attach_panels (interactive.py:291-296) and a second allocation branch at its bottom (:338-340); attach_reviewer_panel raises if the pane already exists (:371-372) where PR 9/10 return the mapping. _decide rewrites the reviewer's verdict to "blocked" in review.json (:282), so the persisted record differs from what the reviewer wrote (original kept only in receipt["decision"]). Worktree/evidence checks are still duplicated between _accept_native and _review_print. The completion contract is a hand-written JSON schema with no v1.ts/examples/contract test, against the repo's contracts:export convention. write_private/prompt.txt (interactive.py:181-182, :213, :241) is slice-C material in the shared file.
data.ranking_reason: PR 10 is the codebase I would rather own in six months: reconcile()/launch() and finish_review() mean the worker and reviewer lifecycles and the two transports each have exactly one implementation, the node identity is a single string plus a label map, and its rough edges (dead stop-marker shortcut, dead-trigger review_resumable, triple-stated default) are small and local. PR 11 achieves the same DRY split and adds the best validators and the only correct bounded-retry design, but a maintainer must hold four interrupt states across review_candidate/_review_native/_accept_native, hunt magic "review" strings that pipeline.py spells as a constant, and reason about a non-idempotent pane attach; that is more code to keep correct. PR 9 is last because it did not generalise the core: run_reviewer is a copy of run(), acceptance is copied three times, the reviewer/review dual identity needs file_prefix() to bridge it, and it ships a behavioural bug (resolved P0/P1 blocks an approved verdict) that PR 10 and 11 both fixed.

findings.title: native_review blocks an approved verdict that carries a resolved P0/P1, contradicting its own contract
findings.detail: read_review_completion enforces the v1.ts cross-field rule that only an UNRESOLVED P0/P1 invalidates an approval, and Pipeline.validate_review accepts resolved P0/P1, but native_review then re-checks severity alone and raises 'Independent reviewer blocked the candidate'. A reviewer who records a P1 as resolved and approves gets the run blocked. PR 10 (finish_review) and PR 11 (blocking_findings) both fixed this; PR 9 kept the baseline check while adding a contract that makes it wrong.
findings.evidence: md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:272 `if decision["verdict"] != "approved" or any(item["severity"] in {"P0", "P1"} for item in decision["findings"]): raise RuntimeError("Independent reviewer blocked the candidate")` vs :186-190 `if item["verdict"] == "approved" and any(finding["severity"] != "P2" and finding["disposition"] != "resolved" ...)` and contracts/workflow/v1.ts:174-175 'Approval cannot leave an unresolved P0/P1 finding'. Same severity-only check survives in print_review at :323.

findings.title: run_reviewer is a 54-line near-verbatim copy of run(); no reconcile/launch extraction
findings.detail: The reconcile-existing-receipt block and the launch-log/fsync/settle/needs_reconciliation block are duplicated between run() and run_reviewer(). Any future change to how a native session is bound (e.g. the settle poll, the receipt fields, the HERDR_ env scrub) must be made in two places. PR 10 and PR 11 both extracted reconcile()/launch() so their run/run_reviewer are thin.
findings.evidence: md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:187-240 (funclen: run_reviewer 54 lines) repeats interactive.py:112-184 run(): same `receipt.update(status="attached_session_available", background_id=row["id"], session_id=row["sessionId"], observed_state=row["state"], native_started_at=row.get("startedAt"))`, same `with (self.directory / f"...launch.log").open("w") as log: ... os.fsync(log.fileno())`, same `except BaseException as error: receipt.update(status="needs_reconciliation", error=str(error))`. Compare md-manager-high/workflow/interactive.py:117-161 reconcile()/launch() and md-manager-ultra/workflow/interactive.py:113-149.

findings.title: Dual reviewer/review identity bridged by file_prefix() in a module that otherwise rejects the reviewer
findings.detail: REVIEWER = "reviewer" names the pane, launch name, terminals.json key and --node value, while receipts, events, graph node, stop marker and node_id all use "review"; file_prefix() exists solely to map one to the other. The constant lives in sessions.py, whose ClaudeSessions.run still does `if node not in NODES: raise ValueError("Unknown worker")` and whose prepare() never allocates it. PR 10 keeps one identity ("review") with a PANE_LABELS map in interactive.py, the module that owns native sessions.
findings.evidence: md-manager-opus/workflow/sessions.py:20 `REVIEWER = "reviewer"`, :23-25 `def file_prefix(node): return "review" if node == REVIEWER else node`; interactive.py:31-32 receipt_path uses file_prefix; interactive.py:396 `--node choices=[*NODES, REVIEWER]`; RUNBOOK.md:179 `attach-one "$RUN" --node reviewer`; but interactive.py:217 `receipt = {"node_id": "review", ...}` and pipeline.py:158-170 `self.event("review", ...)`. Contrast md-manager-high/workflow/interactive.py:24-26 `REVIEW_NODE = "review"; SESSION_NODES = (*NODES, REVIEW_NODE); PANE_LABELS = {..., REVIEW_NODE: "reviewer"}`.

findings.title: Post-decision acceptance logic duplicated across review_worktree, native_review and print_review
findings.detail: The worktree-clean check, evidence-digest check, review dict construction and validate_review call are written three times (review_worktree's resume path, native_review, print_review). PR 10 has one copy in finish_review; PR 11 has two.
findings.evidence: grep -c '"Evidence changed during review"' automatic.py -> opus 3, high 1, ultra 2; grep -c '"Reviewer worktree changed"' -> opus 3, high 1, ultra 2; grep -c '"independent": True' -> opus 2, high 1, ultra 1. md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:221-225 (review_worktree), :273-278 (native_review), :325-330 (print_review).

findings.title: wait_review treats native state 'blocked' as a quota failure and never stops the reviewer on failure
findings.detail: The reviewer runs with --permission-mode dontAsk (not bypassPermissions like the workers), so a 'blocked' row means it is waiting for a human (a question, or a denied write it reports). PR 9 copies the worker branch and raises with the worker's quota message; PR 10 and PR 11, having run it live, both treat blocked as a waiting state until the deadline and emit an event. Separately, PR 9 only stops the reviewer on success (stop_reviewer called once, at :281), so a blocked verdict or deadline leaves a live session that has --add-dir <run dir> and Write; the handoff documents this as intentional but it diverges from drive()'s worker policy of stopping sessions that cannot continue.
findings.evidence: md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:207-208 `if row["state"] == "blocked": raise RuntimeError("Reviewer blocked; inspect quota or native error. No billing/provider fallback.")`; grep stop_reviewer automatic.py -> only :281. docs/HANDOFF_REVIEWER_PANE.md:58 'A deadline does not stop the reviewer ... stopping it is left to the operator'. Compare md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:202-207 and md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:219-223 (blocked = waiting, event emitted).

findings.title: 'Resumable review' classifiers are keyed on task.error, which LangGraph never records for KeyboardInterrupt; their real trigger re-executes a deterministic failure
findings.detail: Both PRs justify resumable_review/review_resumable as the path by which a Ctrl-C'd review re-enters its running session. The installed LangGraph runner commits a task error only inside `except Exception`, so KeyboardInterrupt leaves the review task pending with no error and the next drive() loop re-invokes it naturally; the classifier is not what makes the (passing) [75,130,75,0] tests work. The only way task.error is set while the receipt is still 'launching'/'running' is an Exception raised in review_candidate's prologue or review_worktree (e.g. validate_bundle or 'Reviewer worktree changed'), and then the classifier returns True and the same failure is re-run on every supervisor restart up to the 45 limit, the opposite of 'ambiguous invocations never replay'. PR 9 also placed it inside advance_failed_checks whose docstring says 'never launches or review'. PR 11 has no such classifier and would fail closed.
findings.evidence: .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/langgraph/pregel/_runner.py:221-223 `self.commit(t, None)` / `except Exception as exc: self.commit(t, exc)`; _runner.py:578-600 commit() only writes ERROR for exceptions it receives. md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:343-352 resumable_review, :355 docstring 'Retry only recorded failing verification packets, never launches or review.' vs :362 `if failures == ["review"]: return resumable_review(runtime)`; test_automatic.py:263-285 builds `SimpleNamespace(name="review", error="interrupted")` synthetically. md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:216-226 review_resumable, :459 wired into drive; `grep -n review_resumable test_automatic.py` -> no direct test.

findings.title: wait_review's stop-marker recovery shortcut is unreachable in the real flow
findings.detail: wait_review starts with 'if review.stop.json says stopped, accept the file bound to the stopped session'. But review_native always calls runtime.sessions.run_reviewer first, which for an existing receipt calls reconcile() -> locate(); for a stopped session locate() returns None or raises 'No live native PID', so run_reviewer raises 'Existing launch cannot be reconciled' before wait_review is ever entered. The branch documents a recovery that cannot happen. PR 11 handles the same scenario correctly by returning early from review_candidate on a succeeded receipt and retrying only the stop.
findings.evidence: md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:194-198 `stop = runtime.directory / f"{REVIEW_NODE}.stop.json"; if stop.exists() and read_json(stop)["stopped"]: return read_review_completion(...)`; review_native order :286 run_reviewer -> :297 wait_review; interactive.py:175-176 `if (...review.interactive.json).exists(): return self.reconcile(REVIEW_NODE)`; reconcile :123-125 `row = self.locate(...); if row is None: raise RuntimeError("Existing launch cannot be reconciled; no automatic relaunch")`. Compare md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:236-241.

findings.title: export_state bumped to 1.2.0 while the adapter still requires z.literal('1.0.0') (outside the slice-A file set, verified)
findings.detail: Not part of the five controller files, but it decides whether the merged branch is usable: any run exported after merging PR 10 is rejected by server/projects.ts until slice B lands. PR 9 leaves export_state untouched; PR 11 updates the adapter to accept 1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0.
findings.evidence: md-manager-high/workflow/export_state.py:16 `EXPORT_VERSION = "1.2.0"`; `git -C md-manager-high diff 61e4752 --stat -- server/ src/` -> empty; md-manager/server/projects.ts:37 `const EXPORT_VERSION = '1.0.0'`, :52 `version: z.literal(EXPORT_VERSION)`. md-manager-ultra/server/projects.ts:44 `const EXPORT_VERSIONS = ['1.0.0', '1.1.0', '1.2.0'] as const`.

findings.title: The missing-key default is stated three ways: DEFAULTS says native, two literals say print
findings.detail: reviewer_transport() and validate_automatic each hard-code "print" as the fallback while DEFAULTS["reviewer_transport"] is "native". The choice itself is the safest of the three PRs for the on-disk run (its plan has no key and was print-reviewed), but a maintainer reading DEFAULTS will 'fix' the getter. PR 9 reads DEFAULTS in one place; PR 11 also hard-codes its literal.
findings.evidence: md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:26 `... "reviewer_transport": "native"}`, :45 `return plan["automatic"].get("reviewer_transport", "print")`, :54 `settings.get("reviewer_transport", "print") not in TRANSPORTS`; :53 `set(settings) - {"reviewer_transport"} != set(DEFAULTS) - {"reviewer_transport"}`. Live plan: ~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/project-workflows/project-workflows-001/plan.json automatic = {finish, permission_mode, worker_timeout_seconds: 3600, review_timeout_seconds: 1800} (no key), review.stdout.json present (print mode). Contrast md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:43-44 `return plan.get("automatic", {}).get("reviewer_transport", DEFAULTS["reviewer_transport"])`.

findings.title: automatic.py now depends on interactive.py panes and bypasses the Pipeline.launch wrapper convention; completion bound to a self-reported session UUID
findings.detail: Baseline layering is sessions -> interactive -> pipeline, with automatic.py using only sessions and the Pipeline runtime; Pipeline.launch(node) wraps sessions.run with events. PR 10 imports REVIEW_NODE and attach_reviewer_pane into automatic.py at module level, calls runtime.sessions.run_reviewer directly and emits the launch/pane events from automatic.py, so the reviewer launch has no Pipeline counterpart to launch(). PR 9 and PR 11 add Pipeline.launch_reviewer mirroring launch(). PR 10 also asks the reviewer to write its own session UUID (reviewer_session) rather than a controller-issued launch_token as the workers do; it worked in the smoke run but relies on the model knowing its own id.
findings.evidence: md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:21 `from .interactive import REVIEW_NODE, attach_reviewer_pane`; :286-296 run_reviewer + runtime.event(REVIEW_NODE, "interactive", ...) + attach_reviewer_pane inside review_native; :159 prompt example `"reviewer_session": "<your own session UUID as shown by `claude agents`; the controller verifies it>"`; :184 `if item["reviewer_session"] != session_id`. Smoke: ~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/smoke/review-smoke-001/review.completion.json reviewer_session 5865c9a6-... == review.interactive.json session_id. Compare md-manager-opus/workflow/pipeline.py:156-171 and md-manager-ultra/workflow/pipeline.py:148-167 Pipeline.launch_reviewer.

findings.title: automatic.py never imports REVIEW and spells the node and its files as ~20 magic strings while pipeline.py uses the constant; label rule duplicated inline
findings.detail: interactive.py defines REVIEW = "review" and pipeline.py imports it, but automatic.py uses literal "review" for locate(), event(), node_id binding and the file names review.interactive.json / review.completion.json / review.stop.json / review.json. A rename or a file-layout change has to be chased through two conventions. The pane/launch label rule 'reviewer' if node == REVIEW else node is also written twice instead of once (PR 10 has PANE_LABELS).
findings.evidence: grep -n '"review' md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py -> :162, :163, :185, :198, :209, :211, :216, :223, :271, :283, :302, :314, :332, :345, :355, :362, :473 (no `from .interactive import REVIEW`; imports at :20-21 are checks/sessions only). md-manager-ultra/workflow/interactive.py:38 `f"workflow-{...}-{'reviewer' if node == REVIEW else node}"` and :353 `f"Claude: {'reviewer' if node == REVIEW else node}"`. Compare md-manager-high/workflow/interactive.py:26 PANE_LABELS used at :41 and :334.

findings.title: Densest control flow of the three: nested resume branch, 15-line KeyboardInterrupt handler that re-reads receipts, BaseException re-raise idiom
findings.detail: review_candidate carries an inline three-way resume decision (succeeded-but-unstopped / running-without-session_id -> reconcile_reviewer with its own error handling / running-with-session -> _accept_native); _review_native's except KeyboardInterrupt reads review.interactive.json to copy session_id/background_id into the review receipt; Pipeline.launch_reviewer catches BaseException, logs, then re-raises only non-Exception, and pre-checks HERDR_ENV although observer.herdr() already guards it. Every branch is tested and the behaviour is arguably the most correct, but a maintainer must hold four interrupt points and two receipts in their head to change any of it. PR 10 handles the same happy path plus Ctrl-C in about half the lines.
findings.evidence: md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:228-260 review_candidate resume block (`if not receipt.get("session_id"): try: bound = runtime.reconcile_reviewer() except Exception as error: receipt.update(status="needs_reconciliation"...)`), :298-316 `except KeyboardInterrupt: issued = runtime.directory / "review.interactive.json" ... bound = read_json(issued); receipt.update({key: bound[key] for key in ("session_id", "background_id") if bound.get(key)}, status="running")`; pipeline.py:156-167 `if (self.directory / "terminals.json").exists() and os.environ.get("HERDR_ENV") == "1": ... except BaseException as error: ... if not isinstance(error, Exception): raise`; observer.py:44-45 already raises when HERDR_ENV != "1". funclen: _accept_native 39, _review_native 32, review_candidate ~45 lines.

findings.title: Hand-written reviewCompletion.schema.json with no v1.ts/examples/contract test breaks the contracts:export convention
findings.detail: Every other schema in contracts/workflow is generated from v1.ts (zod) with examples and contract tests; PR 9 and PR 10 followed that. PR 11's 39-line JSON has no TypeScript source, so the completion contract now has a different source of truth from the rest, and the cross-field rules (blocked-needs-findings, approved-cannot-carry-unresolved-P0/P1) exist only in Python (blocking_findings/_decide), not in the contract package.
findings.evidence: md-manager-ultra/contracts/workflow/reviewCompletion.schema.json (hand-written, `"title": "Review completion signal v1.0.0"`); `grep -c reviewCompletion md-manager-ultra/contracts/workflow/{v1.ts,examples.ts,contract.test.ts}` -> 0,0,0. Compare md-manager-opus/contracts/workflow/v1.ts:94-107 reviewCompletionSchema + :169-177 validateReviewCompletion and md-manager-high/contracts/workflow/v1.ts:110-120.

findings.title: Pane attach split across three functions, a redirect branch inside attach_panels, and a non-idempotent attach_reviewer_panel
findings.detail: attach_panels now begins with 'if a mapping exists and the reviewer is missing, go do the reviewer instead', and ends with a second reviewer-allocation branch; attach_reviewer_panel raises if the reviewer pane already exists, whereas PR 9/10 return the mapping. Pipeline.launch_reviewer swallows that error into a 'not attached' event, so a second call reports a misleading failure rather than a no-op.
findings.evidence: md-manager-ultra/workflow/interactive.py:291-296 `if set(NODES) <= set(mapping) and REVIEW not in mapping and (directory / "review.interactive.json").exists(): return attach_reviewer_panel(sessions)` inside attach_panels; :338-340 second branch `if (directory / "review.interactive.json").exists() and sessions.locate(REVIEW, rows) is not None: allocate_reviewer_pane(...)`; :371-372 `if REVIEW in mapping: raise RuntimeError("Reviewer pane already allocated; ...")`. Compare md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:367-368 `if REVIEWER in mapping: return mapping` and md-manager-high/workflow/interactive.py:349-350.

findings.title: _decide rewrites the reviewer's verdict before persisting review.json
findings.detail: An approved verdict with an unresolved P0/P1 is persisted as verdict "blocked"; the record the viewer shows is no longer what the reviewer wrote (the original survives only in receipt["decision"]). PR 10 persists the verdict verbatim and raises.
findings.evidence: md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:280-283 `blocked = decision["verdict"] != "approved" or bool(blocking_findings(decision["findings"])); if blocked: review["verdict"] = "blocked"  # An approval with an unresolved P0/P1 is contradictory; the run is blocked.` then :284 `save_json(runtime.directory / "review.json", review)`. Compare md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:270-276.

findings.title: Default 'native' for plans lacking reviewer_transport does not describe any real plan; PR 11's docstring claim is unenforced
findings.detail: automatic_settings pins the key on every new plan, so the only plans without it are pre-existing ones, all reviewed in print mode. PR 9 and PR 11 default the getter to native (PR 11's docstring adds 'though they never launch a new reviewer', which nothing enforces: an old plan still at the review step would launch a native reviewer whose preflight never checked --allowedTools). PR 10's 'print' default matches reality; PR 11 at least records the truth in the export via recorded_transport().
findings.evidence: md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:43-44 default DEFAULTS["reviewer_transport"] == "native"; md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:58-60 `"""Effective transport: plans that predate the setting are native, though they never launch a new reviewer.""" return plan["automatic"].get("reviewer_transport", "native")`; md-manager-ultra/workflow/export_state.py:62-76, :147-148 recorded_transport(). Live plan lacks the key and has review.stdout.json (print).

findings.title: Copy-pasted prompt instruction and a new event status vocabulary word
findings.detail: The reviewer prompt tells a Write-only session (no Bash) to write 'atomically (temporary file then rename)', copied from the worker completion_prompt where Bash exists; PR 11 explicitly says the opposite because its allow-rule is path-specific. Pipeline.launch_reviewer also introduces a new event status 'detached'; the adapter tolerates unknown statuses (maps to null) but it is a new word in the timeline vocabulary that no contract or viewer knows.
findings.evidence: md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:168 `"atomically (temporary file then rename) to "` (reviewer) vs :69 (worker); interactive.py:196 `reviewer_tools = "Read,Glob,Grep,Write"`. pipeline.py:170 `self.event("review", "detached", f"No reviewer pane: {error}")`; md-manager/server/projects.ts:128-130 EVENT_STATUS has no 'detached', :558 `EVENT_STATUS[event.status] ?? null`. md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:174-175 'It cannot be written under a temporary name and renamed'.

findings.title: write_private/prompt.txt evidence added to the shared interactive.py surface as part of slice A
findings.detail: Persisting worker and reviewer prompts is slice C (run inputs) material; PR 11 lands it in the shared launch path. Harmless (three lines) but it widens what slice A touches in the most shared file.
findings.evidence: md-manager-ultra/workflow/interactive.py:181-182 `# The exact prompt is run evidence (the viewer shows it)... write_private(self.directory / f"{node}.prompt.txt", prompt)`, :213 `write_private(self.directory / "review.prompt.txt", prompt)`, :241-243 def write_private.

findings.title: reconcile()/launch() extraction and finish_review are the cleanest generalisation on the shared surface
findings.detail: The common native-session lifecycle exists once: launch() fills node_id/session_id/plan_digest/worktree/status/attempt/launcher_invocations/launch_requested_at and owns the log/fsync/settle/needs_reconciliation handling; run() and run_reviewer() only build a command and a 2-key receipt. finish_review is the single acceptance path for both transports and fixes the baseline's severity-only P0/P1 check. SESSION_NODES/PANE_LABELS keep one identity; launched_nodes() lets status/attach scale to N sessions; attach_reviewer_pane returns None for headless runs instead of throwing.
findings.evidence: md-manager-high/workflow/interactive.py:117-129 reconcile, :131-161 launch (`receipt.update(node_id=node, session_id=None, plan_digest=plan_digest(self.plan), worktree=str(cwd), status="launching", attempt=1, launcher_invocations=1, launch_requested_at=...)`), :163-175 run_reviewer (`receipt = {"launch_token": None, "base_commit": ..., "role": "reviewer", ...}; return self.launch(REVIEW_NODE, cwd, command, receipt)`), :223-225 launched_nodes, :343-352 attach_reviewer_pane `return None`; automatic.py:264-280 finish_review with `any(x["severity"] in {"P0", "P1"} and x["disposition"] != "resolved" ...)`.

findings.title: Reusable validators and a precisely bounded stop-retry are the best-designed pieces in any of the three PRs
findings.detail: blocking_findings and check_review(require_approved) are shared by validate_review, _decide and ExportRuntime, so the finding rules exist once. reviewer_stopped/reviewer_stop_pending guard exactly the one retry that is safe (a durable accept whose stop was not confirmed), drive raises immediately with a resume note and only a resumed controller retries once. The variadic-flag ordering trap is explained at the command builder, and REQUIRED_KEYS/REVIEW_COMPLETION_LIMIT/REVIEWER_TRANSPORTS are named constants.
findings.evidence: md-manager-ultra/workflow/pipeline.py:42-70 blocking_findings/check_review, :382-384 validate_review delegates, :415-440 ExportRuntime reuses check_review(require_approved=False); automatic.py:269-273 reviewer_stopped, :467-478 reviewer_stop_pending, :530-540 drive `if reviewer_stop_pending(runtime, failed): raise RuntimeError(REVIEW_STOP_NOTE.format(...)) from error`; interactive.py:220-223 '--tools, --allowedTools and --add-dir are variadic: any of them directly before the positional prompt would swallow it'; automatic.py:26-28, :141.

findings.title: Single-source transport default, tidy settings validation, and the Pipeline.launch pattern honoured
findings.detail: transport() reads DEFAULTS rather than repeating a literal; validate_automatic uses REQUIRED_SETTINGS <= set(settings) <= set(DEFAULTS); review_worktree/review_instructions/review_completion_prompt are extracted; stop_session returns the intent for callers; attach_reviewer_pane is idempotent; Pipeline.launch_reviewer mirrors Pipeline.launch so events stay in one layer; the completion contract lives in v1.ts with cross-field rules and the Python mirror says so.
findings.evidence: md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:43-44, :49 `not REQUIRED_SETTINGS <= set(settings) <= set(DEFAULTS)`, :214-231 review_worktree, :183 comment 'Cross-field rules mirrored from contracts/workflow/v1.ts'; pipeline.py:112-140 stop_session returns intent, :156-171 launch_reviewer; interactive.py:355-382 attach_reviewer_pane `if REVIEWER in mapping: return mapping`; contracts/workflow/v1.ts:94-107, :169-177.
